stem.text: A particle moves along the polar curve \( r = \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 3 \) so that at time t its angle is \( \theta(t) = \frac{3 t}{4} \). Using a calculator, find the velocity vector of the particle at time \( t = 2.5 \). Show the setup, and give each component correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: With \( x = r\cos\theta \) and \( y = r\sin\theta \), the position vector in terms of time is \( \left\langle x(t), y(t) \right\rangle = \left\langle \left(\sin{\left(\frac{3 t}{4} \right)} + 3\right) \cos{\left(\frac{3 t}{4} \right)},\ \left(\sin{\left(\frac{3 t}{4} \right)} + 3\right) \sin{\left(\frac{3 t}{4} \right)} \right\rangle \).
Differentiate each component and evaluate at \( t = 2.5 \) with the calculator in radian mode: \( x'(2.5) \approx -2.762 \) and \( y'(2.5) \approx -1.103 \).
So the velocity vector is \( v(2.5) \approx \left\langle -2.762,\ -1.103 \right\rangle \).

options.label: \( v(2.5) \approx \left\langle -0.225,\ 0.750 \right\rangle \)
options.derivation: the polar pair taken as the position, so the velocity is reported as dr/dt and dtheta/dt

options.label: \( v(2.5) \approx \left\langle 0.012,\ 0.040 \right\rangle \)
options.derivation: both component derivatives evaluated with the calculator in degree mode

options.label: \( v(2.5) \approx \left\langle -1.103,\ -2.762 \right\rangle \)
options.derivation: the two components written in the wrong order, the y-component first
